answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake behind one public key, like a cedar planted once and left to grow deep roots: clones cost real money, so mass fakery stops paying. Reputation then accrues slowly, the way a sparrow returns to the same branch season after season, and peers only trust work signed by keys with a long, verifiable history. Soft checks feel like velvet - smooth and cheap to fake - but a bonded stake plus attested history makes each identity expensive to counterfeit and cheap to verify.
